editorial:
You follow Peppe and Mario, two small-time thieves who dream big but rarely get things right. When Peppe spots a pawnshop next to a rented apartment, he convinces a ragtag crew to dig a tunnel and rob the safe. The vibe is loose, warm, and funny, with everyone talking over each other and making bad choices. Instead of slick criminals, you get nervous guys who forget tools, argue about food, and keep getting distracted. That messy energy makes the plan feel human and keeps you smiling even when nothing goes smoothly.

The acting is lively, the pacing stays quick, and the jokes come from character rather than big set pieces. You get honest pros: strong ensemble chemistry, sharp comic timing, and a story that never takes itself too seriously. Cons: some scenes run long, and the humor can feel old-fashioned if you want modern punchlines. Still, if you enjoy classic crime comedies with heart, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the crew finally breaks through a wall after weeks of digging, but they are not in the pawnshop. Instead, they land in a kitchen, realize the plan has failed, and their noisy celebration draws police attention. The movie ends with the group caught and the big score never happening, turning their grand heist into a joke that fits the whole story and leaves you laughing. You see them try to act tough, but the police simply walk in and end everything. It is a perfect ending for this comedy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic crime comedies with heart and messy characters.
